[codex] ## Operating Context
[codex] 
[codex] This repository coordinates the deployment and development environment for the Budget Analyzer application, a reference microservices architecture used as an open source learning resource for AI-assisted development.
[codex] 
[codex] This project is designed for AI-assisted development. The containerized development environment lives in the sibling `../workspace` repository; that repo owns the devcontainer configuration.
[codex] 
[codex] The `ext-authz` Go service implementation lives in the sibling `../ext-authz`
[codex] repository. This orchestration repository owns its Kubernetes manifests, Istio
[codex] `ext_authz` wiring, NGINX integration, Redis ACL wiring, production image
[codex] policy, and deployment documentation.
[codex] 
[codex] The default debugging model is split across host and container:
[codex] - Tilt runs on the host machine
[codex] - AI agents run inside the container
[codex] - The container has shared workspace access and full `kubectl` access to the host-managed cluster
[codex] 
[codex] The agent container is inside the trusted local-development boundary. Local
[codex] workspace files, the local Kind kubeconfig and Kubernetes Secrets, generated
[codex] development TLS keys, and disposable local API-test credentials are not hidden
[codex] from the agent. Never expose staging or production kubeconfigs, cloud or
[codex] deployment credentials, user credentials, or session cookies to this
[codex] container, and never use an agent session to deploy or administer staging or
[codex] production. Before an in-container agent-authorized cluster mutation, require
[codex] the current context and referenced cluster to equal `kind-kind`, require a
[codex] loopback Kubernetes API endpoint, and require the `kind-control-plane` node.
[codex] Use `kind get clusters` only as an additional host-side check because the
[codex] container Docker daemon cannot enumerate the host-managed Kind cluster. For
[codex] the full boundary and API-test target checks, read
[codex] `docs/architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md` before changing agent sandbox,
[codex] credential, Kubernetes-access, or autonomous execution behavior.
[codex] 
[codex] Production target is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Free Tier on ARM64:
[codex] - Shape: `VM.Standard.A1.Flex`
[codex] - Capacity: 4 OCPUs, 24 GB RAM
[codex] - OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 Minimal
[codex] - Region baseline: Phoenix
[codex] - Deployment model: single-node, production-grade demo environment
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture implications:
[codex] - All container images must support `linux/arm64`
[codex] - Local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s are both treated as production-grade deployment paths
[codex] - Observability remains internal-only in both environments
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture principles:
[codex] - Production parity between local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Microservices with clear service boundaries and independent deployability
[codex] - Session-based edge authorization for browser security and session management
[codex] - Istio ingress handles ext_authz and auth-path throttling; NGINX handles API routing, backend/API rate limiting, and load balancing
[codex] - Resource-based routing keeps the frontend decoupled from service topology
[codex] - Defense in depth across Istio ingress, Session Gateway or NGINX, and downstream services
[codex] - Kubernetes-native development uses Tilt live update so code changes reach running pods quickly while the full security stack stays active; see `docs/development/local-environment.md#live-development-pipeline`
[codex] 
[codex] Technology pattern:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application
[codex] - Backends: Spring Boot + Java + Gradle
[codex] - Browser auth edge: Session Gateway (Spring WebFlux)
[codex] - External authorization: `ext-authz` Go service
[codex] - Edge and routing: Istio ingress/egress plus NGINX API gateway
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Kiali
[codex] 
[codex] Service topology summary:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application for browser clients
[codex] - Backend workloads: Spring Boot microservices behind NGINX, plus Session Gateway and `ext-authz` on the auth and authorization path
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ in the `infrastructure` namespace; Redis `/data` is PVC-backed through the `redis-data` claim template
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, kube-state-metrics, the repo-managed Jaeger v2 backend, and standalone Kiali in `monitoring`; Jaeger and Kiali stay `ClusterIP`-only
[codex] - Ingress and egress: Istio ingress handles browser entry, `ext_authz`, and auth-path throttling; Istio egress stays `ClusterIP` with `REGISTRY_ONLY`
[codex] - Exact service ports and exposure rules live in `docs/architecture/port-reference.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Adding a new service:
[codex] - Create manifests in `kubernetes/services/{name}/`
[codex] - Register the service in `Tiltfile`
[codex] - Add NGINX routes when the service owns public resources
[codex] - See `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `nginx/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Version numbers and concrete dependency selections live in service repos, manifests, and checked-in release inputs, not in this file.
[codex]

[codex] ## Core Runtime Pattern
[codex] 
[codex] The primary request flow is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Browser -> Istio Ingress -> ext_authz validates session -> NGINX -> services
[codex] Auth paths -> Istio Ingress -> Session Gateway
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Entry-point ownership:
[codex] - Browser auth lifecycle stays on the direct Session Gateway lane
[codex] - API traffic stays on the NGINX lane with ingress-layer `ext_authz`
[codex] - Exact route ownership and `/api-docs` behavior live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `docs-aggregator/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Session and identity rules:
[codex] - Session Gateway resolves roles and permissions from `permission-service` during session creation and owns browser session lifecycle on the direct auth lane
[codex] - Keep browser session logic on the direct `/auth/*` lane rather than pushing it through the general API path
[codex] - Exact browser endpoints and the shared Session Gateway/`ext_authz` contract live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Operational guardrails:
[codex] - Follow the resource-based routing pattern for new API endpoints
[codex] - Treat any new public `/api/...` route as incomplete until both `nginx/nginx.k8s.conf` and `nginx/nginx.production.k8s.conf` claim it and verification proves it does not fall through to the SPA
[codex] - Keep Spring Boot workloads on the startup/readiness/liveness probe pattern used by the checked-in manifests
[codex] - Keep PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, and Redis on their repo-owned stateful deployment patterns
[codex] - Redis `/data` is PVC-backed. Do not treat pod replacement or `tilt down` as a Redis reset. Use `./scripts/ops/flush-redis.sh` for a logical reset, or recreate the cluster/runtime when a full clean state is required
[codex] 
[codex] Observability rules:
[codex] - Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali are internal-only in both local Tilt and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Use loopback-only access for operators: raw `kubectl port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 ...` or `./scripts/ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh`
[codex] - `./scripts/smoketest/verify-observability-port-forward-access.sh` is the focused access proof
[codex] - Do not introduce public observability hostnames
[codex] - Do not use `--address 0.0.0.0` for observability access
[codex] - Exact observability access commands, local ports, and Kiali auth flow live in `docs/architecture/observability.md`
[codex]

[codex] # Documentation Ownership
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Active
[codex] **Purpose:** Define the canonical owner for recurring documentation topics so
[codex] exact operational detail lives in one place and non-owner docs summarize and
[codex] link instead of copying.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - One recurring topic should have one canonical owner.
[codex] - Non-owner docs may give a short summary, orientation paragraph, or diagram,
[codex]   but they should not own the full command sequence, table, or contract.
[codex] - When a topic changes, update the owner doc first, then update summaries,
[codex]   indexes, and cross-links that point to it.
[codex] - `docs/archive/` is historical reference only and does not own active
[codex]   implementation detail.
[codex] - If no existing owner fits a new recurring topic, choose one and update this
[codex]   file in the same change.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact Detail vs. Summary
[codex] 
[codex] In this repo, "exact detail" includes things such as:
[codex] 
[codex] - full startup and verifier sequences
[codex] - complete port tables
[codex] - observability access commands
[codex] - detailed route ownership lists
[codex] - detailed `/api-docs` behavior and output definitions
[codex] 
[codex] Those details should live in the owner doc. Non-owner docs can summarize the
[codex] shape of the topic and link outward.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership Map
[codex] 
[codex] | Topic | Canonical owner | Rule for non-owner docs |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Documentation ownership policy | [docs/OWNERSHIP.md](OWNERSHIP.md) | Link here instead of restating the full ownership map. |
[codex] | AI instructions and repo guardrails | [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) | Other docs may describe the repo, but agent instructions and repo-operating constraints belong there. |
[codex] | Reusable `AGENTS.md` authoring standard | [docs/agents-md-checkstyle.md](agents-md-checkstyle.md) | Link here instead of restating the pattern-based authoring rules. |
[codex] | Release/deployment operating model and terminology | [docs/ci-cd.md](ci-cd.md) | Deployment docs and runbooks may summarize the modes, but source tags, artifact versions, `service-common` versions, image digests, and desired-state manifest terminology belong there. |
[codex] | OCI release deployment checklist and run log template | [docs/runbooks/oci-release-deployment-checklist.md](runbooks/oci-release-deployment-checklist.md) | Link to the template instead of copying the evidence table into plans or deployment docs. |
[codex] | Dependency automation operating policy | [docs/dependency-automation.md](dependency-automation.md) | Keep activation, cost, bot ownership, and triage detail there; the rollout plan owns implementation phases and the preserved review remains the historical benchmark. |

[codex] ## `AGENTS.md` Special Case
[codex] 
[codex] `AGENTS.md` is intentionally rich direct AI context. It is the canonical source
[codex] for repo guardrails, execution constraints, and orchestration-specific working
[codex] rules.
[codex] 
[codex] It is not the canonical owner for every exact operational detail it mentions.
[codex] When `AGENTS.md` references setup flows, ports, observability access, routing,
[codex] or `/api-docs` behavior, prefer a stable summary plus a pointer to the owner
[codex] doc above instead of maintaining a second full inventory there.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Maintenance Workflow
[codex] 
[codex] When a recurring topic changes:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Update the canonical owner doc first.
[codex] 2. Update summaries, indexes, and cross-links that mention the topic.
[codex] 3. Remove or shorten any duplicated exact detail that now conflicts with the
[codex]    owner doc.
[codex] 4. If ownership changed, update this file in the same change.
[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] 
[codex] This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] [September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] [dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership and policy
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared policy is
[codex] [`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] 
[codex] Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] or upstream support status.
[codex] 
[codex] The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] 
[codex] - historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] - local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex]   inventories
[codex] - first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex]   overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] - Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] - arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cost and service boundary
[codex] 
[codex] Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] `govulncheck`.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Activation procedure
[codex] 
[codex] Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] prepared and locally validated their files. Phases 1–11 require no credentials;
[codex] all authenticated validation and credential review belong to Phase 12. Agents
[codex] must never receive GitHub, package, registry, or Mend credentials, including in
[codex] Phase 12. The user performs authenticated operations in GitHub/Mend or their own
[codex] trusted environment and supplies sanitized evidence for agent review.
[codex] 
[codex] Missing authentication, authenticated-only API access, and unauthenticated API
[codex] rate limits are recorded as pending Phase 12 evidence; they do not block local
[codex] configuration preparation. This includes private Maven resolution, complete
[codex] remotely resolved Java snapshots, graph submission, published-preset resolution,
[codex] and hosted bot/scanner runs. Local schema validation, extraction, workflow lint,
[codex] and checks that can run without credentials remain required. Preserve actual
[codex] failures and incomplete outputs; never report a deferred check as passed or
[codex] weaken a hosted job's failure behavior. Non-authentication prerequisites and
[codex] implementation defects remain blockers under the owning repository's rules.
[codex] 
[codex] For each deferred check, record the repository, check/command, affected packages
[codex] or configurations, observed failure or reason not attempted, and the Phase 12
[codex] operator action and expected proof. Sibling phases keep this handoff in their
[codex] own docs and link here; Phase 12 consolidates it in the coverage report.
[codex] 
[codex] The Phase 12 operator sequence is:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex]    free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex]    Maven lookup within its job limits. Complete this before publication can
[codex]    trigger any prepared push workflows.
[codex] 2. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex]    consumer configurations.
[codex] 3. Manually dispatch
[codex]    `dependency-automation-config.yml` with `run_hosted_dry_run` enabled. Its
[codex]    GitHub-provided job token has read permissions only, Renovate runs with
[codex]    `--dry-run=full`, and the user retains control of the trigger. Preserve the
[codex]    workflow URL and confirm that the published preset resolves before proceeding;
[codex]    never copy the job token into an agent environment.
[codex] 4. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex]    rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] 5. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex]    updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] 6. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex]    and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex]    expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] 7. Run each Java repository's graph-submission workflow on its trusted default
[codex]    branch using its existing scoped package-read secrets and a separate GitHub
[codex]    job token for submission. Verify complete application/runtime/test dependency
[codex]    coverage and GitHub acceptance for every repo. A successful ordinary build,
[codex]    package-access preflight, or partial snapshot is insufficient. Preserve a
[codex]    sanitized snapshot or equivalent detailed graph evidence with the run URL and
[codex]    source revision; the orchestration-only Renovate dry run does not prove Maven
[codex]    resolution or Java submission. Resolve every other deferred authenticated
[codex]    lookup/build/scan and retain its evidence too.
[codex] 8. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex]    extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex]    message before enabling consumers.
[codex] 9. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex]    false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex]    and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] 
[codex] The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] 
[codex] Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] 
[codex] - the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] - the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] - a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] - a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] - Trivy CLI/database and registry-resolver metadata, database-download logs,
[codex]   and a machine-readable completion status
[codex] 
[codex] A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] `ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] The cert-manager controller/startup refs and Istio CNI/pilot refs are likewise
[codex] tag-only chart output; only their resolved artifact for a particular run is
[codex] exact. The cert-manager ACME solver input does retain its checked-in digest.
[codex] 
[codex] The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] `guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] still fail the job.
[codex] 
[codex] Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] package scan.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access through the Phase 12 operator handoff. During Phases 1–11,
[codex]   record authentication-dependent checks as pending and continue independent local
[codex]   work. Never seek credentials in the agent environment, use Maven Local as proof
[codex]   of remote resolution, drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error. A
[codex]   resolution defect unrelated to authentication still needs investigation.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] ## Phase 1 pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex] # Dependency Automation Coverage
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Orchestration extraction and exact-image workflow prepared;
[codex] hosted observation and cross-repository scanner phases remain pending.
[codex] 
[codex] **Last updated:** 2026-09-06
[codex] 
[codex] This report records observed extraction and lookup behavior. It is not a list
[codex] of desired dependency versions. The preserved
[codex] [dependency review](dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md) remains the
[codex] historical acceptance benchmark, and
[codex] [Dependency Automation](../dependency-automation.md) owns operating policy.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Phase 1 pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Phase 2 exact-image evidence
[codex] 
[codex] After excluding generated `tmp/` output, a Node 24 extraction rerun found 104
[codex] occurrences across 35 package files. The new workflow contributed six native
[codex] GitHub Actions records: checkout, pinned yq, pinned Trivy setup, pinned Trivy
[codex] CLI input, artifact upload, and the runner identity. The native manager owns all
[codex] of them; no scanner-specific custom manager was needed.
[codex] 
[codex] The offline render and YAML extraction path produced 32 distinct
[codex] image/platform targets from checked-in sources: 28 production/controller refs
[codex] for `linux/arm64`, three local-only refs for `linux/amd64`, and the Istio gateway
[codex] chart's unresolved `image: auto` marker. The workflow scans each registry ref
[codex] only after resolving the platform child digest. The `auto` marker is explicitly
[codex] unscannable without the live Istio injector, so the workflow retains it as a
[codex] known gap without turning that expected limitation into a scan error. Unexpected
[codex] render, resolution, database, and Trivy failures do fail. The render included
[codex] controller hooks, the cert-manager solver argument, the Prometheus
[codex] config-reloader argument, and all five explicit monitoring image overrides.
[codex] 
[codex] Representative scans used Trivy `0.74.0` with vulnerability DB version 2,
[codex] updated `2026-09-06 07:00:11 UTC`. These observed artifact digests are evidence
[codex] for this run, not desired-version inputs:
[codex] 
[codex] | Baseline item | Exact platform artifact and inventory evidence | Advisory comparison |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Redis | The checked-in index selected `redis@sha256:d6550289...` for ARM64. Trivy identified Alpine 3.21.7 and 17 OS packages, but did not identify the Redis server binary/version; the only Go binary inventory was `gosu`. | `GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4` is **missing** because the affected Redis application was not inventoried. The scan cannot prove Redis 7.4.8 or remediation. |

[codex] The missing rows remain acceptance gaps, not clean results or false positives.
[codex] Raw inventories, vulnerability JSON, resolver manifests, stderr, and database
[codex] metadata are the authoritative workflow artifacts. Job summaries deliberately
[codex] separate OS-package and application-package counts and identify mutable source
[codex] refs; they do not infer embedded versions from tags.

[codex] ## Critical Conventions (Always Apply)
[codex] 
[codex] **These rules apply to ALL code changes. No judgment call needed.**
[codex] 
[codex] ### DTO Naming
[codex] - **API request/response classes**: `*Request`, `*Response` (e.g., `CreateTransactionRequest`, `TransactionResponse`)
[codex] - **NEVER use**: `*Dto`, `*DTO`, `*dto` — these suffixes are forbidden
[codex] - **Internal projections**: `*Projection` for JPA projections, `*View` for read models
[codex] 
[codex] ### Variable Naming
[codex] - **Class-level fields**: Use the full class name, not abbreviations
[codex]   - ✅ `private final TransactionRepository transactionRepository;`
[codex]   - ❌ `private final TransactionRepository repository;`
[codex]   - ❌ `private final TransactionRepository txnRepo;`
[codex] - **Local variables**: `var` is preferred, short names acceptable for limited scope
[codex]

[codex] ## Purpose
[codex] 
[codex] Multi-module Gradle project providing shared dependency platforms and runtime libraries for all Budget Analyzer Spring Boot microservices. Publishes four artifacts:
[codex] 
[codex] **spring-platform**: Base backend Spring dependency platform (Spring Boot BOM, Spring Modulith BOM, shared JVM constraints)
[codex] **spring-cloud-platform**: Opt-in Spring Cloud dependency platform overlay
[codex] **service-core**: Minimal-dependency core utilities (base entities, CSV parsing, safe logging)
[codex] **service-web**: Spring Boot web components (exception handling, API error responses, HTTP logging, OpenAPI config)
[codex] 
[codex] **Impacts**: Current consumers are discoverable from the workspace, and changes here affect all services that depend on these libraries.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Module Architecture
[codex] 
[codex] ### spring-platform
[codex] **Location**: `spring-platform/build.gradle.kts`
[codex] 
[codex] **Purpose**: Base Maven BOM-style dependency platform for Budget Analyzer Spring services
[codex] 
[codex] **Contains**:
[codex] - Spring Boot dependency BOM import
[codex] - Spring Modulith dependency BOM import
[codex] - Shared constraints for SpringDoc, Testcontainers, WireMock, Awaitility, and ShedLock
[codex] 
[codex] **Behavior**: Version management only. No source code, runtime dependencies, beans, or autoconfiguration metadata.
[codex] 
[codex] ### spring-cloud-platform
[codex] **Location**: `spring-cloud-platform/build.gradle.kts`
[codex] 
[codex] **Purpose**: Opt-in Maven BOM-style dependency platform for services using Spring Cloud APIs
[codex] 
[codex] **Contains**:
[codex] - spring-platform import
[codex] - Spring Cloud dependency BOM import
[codex] 
[codex] **Behavior**: Version management only. Use only in services that explicitly depend on Spring Cloud libraries.
[codex] 
[codex] ### service-core
[codex] **Location**: `service-core/src/main/java/org/budgetanalyzer/core/`
[codex] 
[codex] **Purpose**: Domain-agnostic utilities with minimal dependencies
[codex] 
[codex] **Contains**:
[codex] - `domain/` - Base JPA entities (AuditableEntity, SoftDeletableEntity)
[codex] - `repository/` - Repository utilities (SoftDeleteOperations)
[codex] - `csv/` - CSV parsing (CsvParser, CsvData, OpenCsvParser)
[codex] - `logging/` - Safe logging utilities (`SafeLogger`, `@Sensitive`, `QueryParamSanitizer`, `HttpBodyLogSanitizer`, `SensitiveHeaderMasker`)
[codex] 
[codex] **Dependencies**: Spring Data JPA, Spring Boot Actuator, Jackson, SLF4J, OpenCSV
[codex] 
[codex] ### service-web
[codex] **Location**: `service-web/src/main/java/org/budgetanalyzer/service/`
[codex] 
[codex] **Purpose**: Spring Boot web components supporting both servlet and reactive stacks
[codex] 
[codex] **Contains**:
[codex] - `api/` - Shared error response models (ApiErrorResponse, ApiErrorType, FieldError, ApiExceptionHandler)
[codex] - `exception/` - Exception hierarchy (shared by both stacks: ResourceNotFoundException, BusinessException, etc.)
[codex] - `config/` - Shared configuration (HttpLoggingProperties, ServiceWebAutoConfiguration, BaseOpenApiConfig)
[codex] - `servlet/` - Servlet-specific implementations (Spring MVC)
[codex]   - `http/` - HTTP filters (CorrelationIdFilter, HttpLoggingFilter, ContentLoggingUtil, HttpLoggingConfig)
[codex]   - `api/` - Exception handler (ServletApiExceptionHandler)
[codex] - `reactive/` - Reactive-specific implementations (Spring WebFlux)
[codex]   - `http/` - Reactive filters (ReactiveCorrelationIdFilter, ReactiveHttpLoggingFilter, body caching decorators, ReactiveHttpLoggingConfig)
[codex]   - `api/` - Exception handler (ReactiveApiExceptionHandler)
[codex] 
[codex] **Dependencies**: service-core (transitive), Spring Boot Starter Web (compileOnly), Spring Boot Starter WebFlux (compileOnly), SpringDoc OpenAPI (compileOnly)
[codex] 
[codex] **Note**: service-web supports BOTH servlet and reactive stacks through conditional autoconfiguration.
[codex] 
[codex] **Note**: Actuator comes from service-core, available to all services (web and non-web).
[codex] 
[codex] **Note**: service-web transitively includes service-core, so consuming services typically only need service-web.
[codex] 
[codex] **Discovery**:
[codex] ```bash
[codex] # View platform build definitions
[codex] cat spring-platform/build.gradle.kts
[codex] cat spring-cloud-platform/build.gradle.kts
[codex] 
[codex] # View published modules configured for this build
[codex] cat settings.gradle.kts
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ## When to Use These Libraries
[codex] 
[codex] - ✅ Cross-service utilities (logging, error handling, common DTOs)
[codex] - ✅ Shared Spring Boot configurations
[codex] - ✅ Common dependencies and version management
[codex] - ❌ Service-specific business logic (belongs in service repos)
[codex] 
[codex] ### Which Module to Depend On?
[codex] 
[codex] **Servlet service with database (most common):**
[codex] ```kotlin
[codex] dependencies {
[codex]     implementation(platform("org.budgetanalyzer:spring-platform:&lt;service-common-version>"))
[codex]     implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web")
[codex]     implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-jpa")
[codex]     implementation("org.budgetanalyzer:service-web:&lt;service-common-version>")
[codex] }
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Reactive service (e.g., Session Gateway):**
[codex] ```kotlin
[codex] dependencies {
[codex]     implementation(platform("org.budgetanalyzer:spring-platform:&lt;service-common-version>"))
[codex]     implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webflux")
[codex]     implementation("org.budgetanalyzer:service-web:&lt;service-common-version>")
[codex] }
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Spring Cloud service:**
[codex] ```kotlin
[codex] dependencies {
[codex]     implementation(platform("org.budgetanalyzer:spring-cloud-platform:&lt;service-common-version>"))
[codex]     implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web")
[codex]     implementation("org.budgetanalyzer:service-web:&lt;service-common-version>")
[codex] }
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Non-web service (batch jobs, workers):**
[codex] ```kotlin
[codex] dependencies {
[codex]     implementation(platform("org.budgetanalyzer:spring-platform:&lt;service-common-version>"))
[codex]     implementation("org.budgetanalyzer:service-core:&lt;service-common-version>")
[codex] }
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Use the checked-in version literal from `build.gradle.kts` when consuming the
[codex] published artifacts.
[codex] 
[codex] **Why explicit dependencies?** Web stack and JPA are `compileOnly` in service-common to prevent classpath conflicts (reactive inheriting servlet) and unnecessary transitive dependencies (reactive services inheriting JPA). Platform artifacts manage versions only; consuming services must still declare the libraries they use.

[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared Budget Analyzer preset. Renovate's native
[codex] Gradle, Gradle Wrapper, and GitHub Actions managers discover this repository's
[codex] version catalog, build scripts, wrapper distribution, and workflow actions.
[codex] There are currently no Dockerfiles in this repository. Add file-specific
[codex] manager configuration only if a future dependency declaration is not covered
[codex] by a native manager.
[codex] 
[codex] The Phase 3 local extraction found 52 dependency occurrences across 12 files:
[codex] 33 Gradle occurrences in seven files, one wrapper occurrence, and 18 GitHub
[codex] Actions occurrences in four workflows. Maven and Gradle lookups produced 41
[codex] candidate branches before scheduling, concurrency limits, and dashboard
[codex] approval. Maintained-line and later-major proposals were both visible for the
[codex] Spring platform, documentation, test, locking, and wrapper dependencies. The
[codex] Actions references were extracted, but authenticated GitHub lookups remain a
[codex] post-publication hosted check because no GitHub token is supplied to local
[codex] validation.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate proposes changes only to direct declarations. It does not turn every
[codex] version inherited from the Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, or Spring Modulith BOMs
[codex] into an independently updateable declaration. The resolved dependency graph
[codex] described below is the security inventory for those inherited versions.
[codex] 
[codex] Major updates remain visible in the Dependency Dashboard and require approval.
[codex] In particular, Spring Boot 4 and the related Spring Cloud, Spring Framework,
[codex] Spring Security, Spring Modulith, SpringDoc, Testcontainers, ShedLock, and test
[codex] platform lines are a compatibility migration, not a routine patch. Renovate
[codex] cannot select the correct release-train combination or coordinate consumer
[codex] services by itself.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Resolved dependency graph
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,
[codex] weekly, and by manual dispatch. The job runs only for the `main` ref and uses
[codex] the official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` action with the open-source
[codex] `basic` cache provider. Its job token receives only `contents: write`, which is
[codex] required by GitHub's Dependency Submission API. The graph is submitted
[codex] directly and is not retained as a workflow artifact or published as a Build
[codex] Scan.
[codex] 
[codex] The action's default resolution task visits all projects and all resolvable
[codex] configurations. Do not add project or configuration filters without proving
[codex] equivalent coverage: the platform modules contribute imported BOMs, while the
[codex] library modules contribute compile, runtime, and test dependency trees.
[codex] 
[codex] Local Phase 3 validation generated an official plugin snapshot without
[codex] submitting it. The snapshot contained 216 resolved coordinate/version entries
[codex] across the four subprojects. It included the Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, and
[codex] Spring Modulith BOM coordinates and these inherited component families where
[codex] the current build actually resolves them:
[codex] 
[codex] | Component family | Resolution evidence |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Spring Framework | Library runtime and test classpaths |
[codex] | Spring Security | `service-core` and `service-web` test classpaths; compile-only APIs are also resolved through compile classpaths |
[codex] | Embedded Tomcat | `service-web` test runtime, which exercises the servlet stack |
[codex] | Netty | `service-web` test runtime, which exercises the reactive stack |
[codex] | Jackson | `service-core` and `service-web` runtime and test classpaths |
[codex] 
[codex] The entry count and resolved versions will change as the checked-in dependency
[codex] selection changes; they are evidence from onboarding, not a desired-version
[codex] inventory. A successful local snapshot proves generation and transitive
[codex] coverage, but only a hosted run after repository activation proves submission
[codex] and creates Dependabot alert input.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub's dependency graph reports resolved packages but does not decide which
[codex] BOM or override should remediate an inherited finding. A Dependabot alert is
[codex] also not proof that an available Spring Boot update fixes every Framework,
[codex] Security, Jackson, Tomcat, or Netty advisory. Trace the affected configuration
[codex] with Gradle dependency insight and review any override as a service-owner
[codex] decision.
[codex]

[codex] Maven Local, omit configurations, or enable a hosted Build Scan to make the job
[codex] pass.

[codex] ## Operating Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - Do not use agent or subagent tools for code exploration. Inspect the workspace
[codex]   directly with `rg`, `find`, and file reads.
[codex] - Never run Git write commands, including `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `reset`,
[codex]   or branch manipulation, unless the user explicitly requests them. The user
[codex]   controls Git operations.
[codex] - Keep implementations simple. Choose the most direct design that handles
[codex]   realistic inputs, states, and failure modes without weakening security, data
[codex]   integrity, or required behavior.
[codex] - Put request shape and syntax validation at the API boundary. Put business
[codex]   invariants, ownership, persistence state, and cross-entity rules in services.
[codex] - Do not duplicate validation across layers unless another caller can bypass the
[codex]   validated boundary or the service owns the rule.
[codex] - Add defensive branches only for states that can plausibly arise and have a
[codex]   useful response. Handle failures at external and asynchronous boundaries
[codex]   explicitly.
[codex] - Never commit credentials or replace missing infrastructure, credentials, or
[codex]   shared artifacts with hard-coded workarounds.
[codex]

[codex] ## Architecture and Security Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - Keep controllers thin and delegate application behavior to services.
[codex]   Controllers must never import repositories.
[codex] - Keep consumers thin and delegate to services. Consumers must never import
[codex]   repositories.
[codex] - Keep transaction boundaries in the service layer and persistence behind
[codex]   repositories.
[codex] - Use Jakarta Persistence APIs only. Never import `org.hibernate.*` or depend on
[codex]   Hibernate-specific behavior.
[codex] - Extend the shared auditable or soft-deletable base entity that matches the
[codex]   domain lifecycle; consult the shared Spring Boot conventions before creating
[codex]   an entity.
[codex] - Access external exchange-rate systems through `ExchangeRateProvider`. The
[codex]   service layer must never reference FRED-specific clients or types.
[codex] - Publish domain events from services. Do not inject message publishers into
[codex]   services; bridge domain events to external messages in listeners.
[codex] - Apply `@SchedulerLock` to scheduled work that must execute once across pods.
[codex] - Cache read paths only where the documented cache strategy calls for it, and
[codex]   evict affected cache entries after imports or mutations.
[codex] - Preserve claims-header-based authorization and enforce endpoint permissions
[codex]   with `@PreAuthorize`. Do not trust client-supplied identity or permission
[codex]   headers outside the platform's validated gateway path.
[codex] - Treat role definitions and atomic permission ownership as permission-service
[codex]   concerns. Do not redefine the ecosystem RBAC model in this repository.
[codex]

[codex]   them.

[codex] - Keep reusable test values in the repository's test fixtures or constants
[codex]   instead of scattering magic values.

[codex] ## Resolved dependency graph
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,
[codex] weekly, and by manual dispatch. The job runs only for the `main` ref and uses
[codex] the official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` action with the open-source
[codex] `basic` cache provider. It resolves all projects and all resolvable
[codex] configurations so application, runtime, build, and test dependency trees are
[codex] included. Do not add configuration filters without proving equivalent coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Remote resolution uses `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_USERNAME` and
[codex] `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN`, exposed to Gradle as `GITHUB_ACTOR` and
[codex] `GITHUB_TOKEN`. These package-read credentials are distinct from
[codex] `${{ github.token }}`, which the action uses to submit the graph with the job's
[codex] only elevated permission, `contents: write`. The snapshot is submitted directly
[codex] and is not retained as an artifact or published as a Build Scan.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow must fail when package credentials are missing, the pinned

[codex] ## Operating Rules
[codex] 
[codex] ### Repository and Git Safety
[codex] 
[codex] - Never run git write operations such as `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `reset`,
[codex]   branch manipulation, or history rewriting unless the user explicitly asks.
[codex] - Do not write outside this repository. Surface required sibling-repository
[codex]   changes instead of making them.
[codex] - Stop and report a missing prerequisite or an authority-boundary conflict. Do
[codex]   not invent a workaround.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Java and Spring Architecture
[codex] 
[codex] - Follow the shared layered architecture: controllers own HTTP concerns,
[codex]   services own business rules and transactions, repositories own data access,
[codex]   and entities carry persistence state.
[codex] - Use `AuditableEntity` and `SoftDeletableEntity` according to the shared entity
[codex]   decision rules. Keep pure association rows simple when row existence is the
[codex]   business fact.
[codex] - Use the shared `ServletApiExceptionHandler` and exception hierarchy for
[codex]   consistent error responses.
[codex] - Name API models `*Request` and `*Response`; never use `*Dto` or `*DTO`.
[codex] - Use provider-independent identifiers in `{prefix}_{full-uuid-hex}` form.
[codex] - Import persistence APIs from `jakarta.persistence.*`; never use
[codex]   `org.hibernate.*` APIs.
[codex] - Apply the Java quality rules for `var`, full variable names, explicit imports,
[codex]   and Javadoc punctuation from the required code-quality document.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Architectural Simplicity
[codex] 
[codex] - Choose the simplest implementation that correctly handles realistic inputs,
[codex]   states, and failure modes. Do not trade away security, data integrity, or
[codex]   required behavior for brevity.
[codex] - Put validation in the layer that owns the rule: request models and
[codex]   controllers validate request shape and syntax; services validate business
[codex]   invariants, ownership, persistence state, and cross-entity rules.
[codex] - Do not duplicate API validation in the service layer when every caller passes
[codex]   through the validated API contract. Validate again only when another caller
[codex]   can bypass that boundary or the service owns the rule.
[codex] - Do not add guards, fallbacks, custom exception paths, abstractions, or
[codex]   extension points for states that enforced boundaries make impossible.
[codex] - Handle plausible failures explicitly at external and asynchronous boundaries.
[codex] - Before adding a defensive branch, identify how the state can arise and what
[codex]   the caller or system can usefully do in response. Omit the branch if neither
[codex]   is concrete.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Security
[codex] 
[codex] - Every controller endpoint method must have `@PreAuthorize`.
[codex] - The only exception is
[codex]   `InternalPermissionController#getUserPermissions`, which is protected by the
[codex]   narrow `/internal/v1/users/*/permissions` matcher in
[codex]   `PermissionServiceSecurityConfig`. Do not broaden this anonymous
[codex]   claims-header exception; orchestration must continue restricting callers
[codex]   through mesh identity and authorization policy.
[codex] - Use `SecurityContextUtil` to obtain the current user. Do not accept actor
[codex]   identity from a request body or untrusted header in application code.
[codex] - Do not bypass authentication, authorization, persistence, or validation
[codex]   layers as a durable fix.
[codex] - Preserve the deactivation contract: commit the local user-state change before
[codex]   external session revocation, keep transient retry bounded, and keep exhausted
[codex]   revocation safe for the caller to retry. Verify current details in the owner
[codex]   code and configuration before changing this flow.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Roles and Permissions
[codex] 
[codex] - Manage roles, permissions, and role-permission mappings only through Flyway
[codex]   migrations. Do not add a runtime grant surface without an explicit design
[codex]   change.
[codex] - Use `{resource}:{action}` for own-resource permissions and
[codex]   `{resource}:{action}:any` for cross-user scope. Add a scoped permission only
[codex]   when a controller has a real cross-user access requirement; do not pre-create
[codex]   speculative variants.
[codex] - Preserve the grant-time action hierarchy within each scope:
[codex]   - Granting `{resource}:write` also requires `{resource}:read` on the same role.
[codex]   - Granting `{resource}:delete` also requires `{resource}:read` on the same role.
[codex]   - `:write` and `:delete` are independent; neither requires the other.
[codex]   - Before revoking `{resource}:read`, revoke matching `:write` and `:delete` grants.
[codex]   - Apply the same rules independently to `:any` permissions.
[codex] - Do not add runtime permission expansion. Downstream services and UIs rely on
[codex]   literal permission checks against well-formed migration grants.
[codex] - After any migration that adds, grants, or revokes a role permission, remind
[codex]   the user to synchronize
[codex]   `../service-common/service-web/src/main/java/org/budgetanalyzer/service/security/test/ClaimsHeaderTestBuilder.java`.
[codex]   This repository cannot make that required sibling-repository change.
[codex]

[codex] ## Operating Rules
[codex] 
[codex] ### Repository and Git Safety
[codex] 
[codex] - Never run git write operations such as `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `reset`,
[codex]   branch manipulation, or history rewriting unless the user explicitly asks.
[codex] - Do not modify source-controlled files outside this repository. Surface
[codex]   required sibling-repository changes instead of making them.
[codex] - Check every plan or feature for documented prerequisites before
[codex]   implementation. If a required prerequisite is missing, stop and inform the
[codex]   user; do not invent a workaround.
[codex] - Do not bypass authentication, authorization, persistence, validation, or
[codex]   other enforced boundaries as a durable fix.
[codex] - Never log credentials, claims-header values, financial statement contents,
[codex]   import tokens, hashes, or other sensitive financial data.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Java and Spring Architecture
[codex] 
[codex] - Follow the layered architecture: controllers own HTTP concerns, services own
[codex]   business rules and transaction boundaries, repositories own data access, and
[codex]   entities carry persistence state.
[codex] - Use dependency injection, declarative transactions, JPA, shared exception
[codex]   handling, Bean Validation, and structured SLF4J logging according to the
[codex]   shared owner documents.
[codex] - Choose the simplest implementation that correctly handles realistic inputs,
[codex]   states, and failure modes. Do not trade away security, data integrity, or
[codex]   required behavior for brevity.
[codex] - Put request shape and syntax validation in request models and controllers.
[codex]   Put business invariants, ownership, persistence state, and cross-entity rules
[codex]   in services.
[codex] - Do not duplicate API validation in a service when every caller passes through
[codex]   the validated API contract. Validate again only when another caller can
[codex]   bypass that boundary or when the service owns the rule.
[codex] - Do not add guards, fallbacks, custom exception paths, abstractions, or
[codex]   extension points for states that enforced boundaries make impossible.
[codex] - Handle plausible failures explicitly at external or asynchronous boundaries.
[codex]   Before adding a defensive branch, identify how the state can arise and what
[codex]   the caller or system can usefully do in response; omit the branch if neither
[codex]   is concrete.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Persistence Exception
[codex] 
[codex] - Use pure JPA for repository persistence by default. Treat saved-view
[codex]   membership batch insertion as the only approved JDBC exception, and keep it
[codex]   behind the repository interface.
[codex] - For that exception, use JPQL to find existing memberships and use only
[codex]   portable, parameterized insert SQL for the JDBC batch. Preserve the shared
[codex]   pessimistic saved-view lifecycle-lock precondition.
[codex] - Read [saved-views.md](docs/saved-views.md#membership-persistence) before
[codex]   changing the exception or its concurrency assumptions. Do not broaden it to
[codex]   other repositories or arbitrary native queries.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Authorization and Ownership
[codex] 
[codex] - Protect every application controller endpoint with fine-grained
[codex]   `@PreAuthorize` checks. Preserve only the public infrastructure surfaces
[codex]   documented by the active API and shared security configuration.
[codex] - Treat `X-User-Id`, `X-Permissions`, and `X-Roles` as trusted only after the
[codex]   gateway and `ClaimsHeaderSecurityConfig` path has established the Spring
[codex]   Security context. Obtain actor identity from that context, not from request
[codex]   bodies or application-level parsing of untrusted headers.
[codex] - Keep ordinary transaction operations scoped to the authenticated owner.
[codex]   Require the documented `:any` permission for cross-user behavior, and do not
[codex]   make an owner filter effective on self-scoped endpoints.
[codex] - Use `ClaimsHeaderTestBuilder` for per-request authentication in controller
[codex]   tests, following the shared testing patterns.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Transaction and Import Invariants
[codex] 
[codex] - Soft-delete transactions. Never hard-delete them, and keep normal queries
[codex]   restricted to active rows.
[codex] - Keep CSV import configuration-driven. A normal new CSV bank format should be
[codex]   represented by statement-format and parser-revision data rather than new Java
[codex]   parsing code. Use dedicated handlers only for formats, such as specialized
[codex]   PDFs, that require code.
[codex] - Keep the public import identity at the statement-format level; parser
[codex]   revisions remain internal implementation and provenance detail. Preserve
[codex]   ordered, atomic preview-to-batch behavior described by the import owner docs.
[codex] - Test parser or format changes with sanitized real bank exports for every
[codex]   affected format. Do not commit sensitive statement samples.
[codex] - Build advanced transaction search with JPA Specifications. Preserve owner
[codex]   scoping and the documented separation between self-scoped and cross-user
[codex]   search.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Layering Exception
[codex] 
[codex] - Treat the existing `TransactionFilter` service/repository import from
[codex]   `api.request` as the only intentional `service -> api` crossing. It carries
[codex]   Spring MVC query-binding annotations and maps directly to transaction

[codex] ## Resolved dependency graph
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,
[codex] weekly, and by manual dispatch. The job runs only for the `main` ref and uses
[codex] the official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` action with the open-source
[codex] `basic` cache provider. It resolves all projects and all resolvable
[codex] configurations so application, runtime, build, and test dependency trees are
[codex] included. Do not add configuration filters without proving equivalent
[codex] coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Remote resolution uses `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_USERNAME` and
[codex] `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN`, exposed to Gradle as `GITHUB_ACTOR` and
[codex] `GITHUB_TOKEN`. These package-read credentials are distinct from
[codex] `${{ github.token }}`, which the action uses to submit the graph with the job's
[codex] only elevated permission, `contents: write`. The package-access preflight
[codex] checks the exact `spring-platform` and `service-web` artifacts used by this
[codex] service. The snapshot is submitted directly and is not retained as an artifact
[codex] or published as a Build Scan.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow must fail when package credentials are missing, either pinned
[codex] `service-common` artifact cannot be resolved, graph generation is incomplete,
[codex] or GitHub rejects submission. Do not substitute Maven Local, omit an internal
[codex] dependency, filter failed configurations, or treat graph-generation failure as
[codex] a clean security result. A hosted run on `main` is the final proof that GitHub
[codex] accepted the submission and can produce Dependabot alerts from it.
[codex] 
[codex] Local Phase 6 validation ran the official GitHub dependency graph Gradle plugin
[codex] without submitting its output. The generated snapshot contained 91 unique
[codex] coordinates and 12 direct entries. It captured build tooling and independently
[codex] resolvable PDFBox, Jackson, and JUnit entries, but no `org.budgetanalyzer`,

[codex] ## Project Overview
[codex] 
[codex] Session Gateway provides session-based edge authorization for browser-based clients in the Budget Analyzer application.
[codex] 
[codex] **Purpose**: Protects sensitive tokens from browser exposure by managing OAuth2 authorization-code flows server-side and issuing HTTP-only session cookies. Writes session data as Redis hashes that the ext_authz HTTP service reads directly for per-request authorization at the Istio ingress. Sessions slide forward through a frontend heartbeat that operates against local Redis state. Owns the OAuth2 and session lifecycle endpoints, while the frontend owns bare `/login`.
[codex] 
[codex] **Key Responsibilities**:
[codex] - Manages OAuth2/OIDC authorization-code flows with Auth0 for browser clients
[codex] - Fetches user roles and permissions from the permission-service on login
[codex] - Writes session data (userId, roles, permissions, expiry) as Redis hashes (`session:{id}`)
[codex] - Maintains per-user session indexes in Redis (`user_sessions:{userId}`) for targeted revocation
[codex] - The ext_authz HTTP service reads these same hashes for ingress authorization — no separate schema
[codex] - Issues HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite session cookies to browsers
[codex] - Provides session heartbeat (`GET /auth/v1/session`) — extends session TTL based on local Redis state
[codex] - Owns `/oauth2/**`, `/auth/**`, `/login/oauth2/**`, and `/logout`
[codex] - Exposes internal session revocation for permission-service (`DELETE /internal/v1/sessions/users/{userId}`)
[codex]

[codex] - Naming: `*Controller`, `*Service`, `*ServiceImpl`, `*Repository`
[codex] - DTOs: `*Request`, `*Response` — NEVER `*Dto`/`*DTO`
[codex] - Exceptions: `BusinessException` for business rules, `InvalidRequestException` for bad input
[codex] - Logging: SLF4J with structured logging (never log sensitive data)
[codex] - Imports: Use `jakarta.persistence.*` — NEVER `org.hibernate.*`
[codex] 
[codex] ### Architectural Simplicity (KISS)
[codex] 
[codex] **Primary rule: Keep it simple.** Choose the simplest implementation that correctly handles realistic inputs, states, and failure modes. Simplicity must not come at the expense of security, data integrity, or required behavior.
[codex] 
[codex] - Put validation in the layer that owns the rule: request models and controllers validate request shape and syntax; services validate business invariants, ownership, persistence state, and cross-entity rules.
[codex] - Do not duplicate API validation in the service layer when every call reaches the service through the validated API contract. Add service-level validation when another caller can bypass that contract or when the service owns the rule.
[codex] - Do not add a guard, fallback, or custom exception path for a state made impossible by an enforced boundary or invariant.
[codex] - At external or asynchronous boundaries, handle plausible failures explicitly because they are outside the local code's control.
[codex] - Before adding a defensive branch, identify how the state can arise and what the caller or system can usefully do in response. If neither is concrete, omit the branch.
[codex] - Prefer a direct implementation and established project patterns over speculative abstractions or extension points.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Architecture Principles
[codex] 
[codex] - **Defense-in-Depth Security**: Session-based edge authorization in the hybrid architecture (Istio ingress → Session Gateway or NGINX, with ext_authz enforcing `/api/*`)
[codex] - **ext_authz-Based Authorization**: The Istio ingress Envoy proxy calls the ext_authz HTTP service, which reads session hashes directly from Redis and injects X-User-Id/X-Roles/X-Permissions headers into API requests
[codex] - **Token Protection**: IDP tokens are consumed at login time only; nothing from Auth0 is persisted after the session is created. Browser only sees an opaque session cookie
[codex] - **Browser-Only Auth**: Session Gateway exclusively serves browser clients. There is no token exchange or bearer token surface
[codex] - **Behind Istio Ingress**: Browser auth and OAuth2 protocol endpoints reach Session Gateway through Istio ingress; bare `/login` is frontend-owned and served through NGINX
[codex] - **Stateful Sessions**: Redis hashes (`session:{id}`) provide distributed session storage — identity, roles, permissions, expiry — read by both Session Gateway and the ext_authz service
[codex] - **Targeted Session Revocation**: Redis sets (`user_sessions:{userId}`) index all active sessions for a user so permission-service can revoke them without scanning `session:*`
[codex] - **Sliding Sessions**: Frontend heartbeat (`GET /auth/v1/session`) resets session TTL based on local Redis state. Session Gateway extends unconditionally on every heartbeat call; the frontend is responsible for calling only when the user is active (idle users = no heartbeat = session expires naturally). Auth0 is not contacted during heartbeat
[codex] 
[codex] ## Service Architecture
[codex] 
[codex] **Pattern**: Session-Based Edge Authorization + OAuth2 Client
[codex] 
[codex] **Architecture Flow**:
[codex] ```text
[codex] Browser → Istio Ingress (:443)
[codex]   ├─ /oauth2/*, /auth/*, /login/oauth2/*, /logout
[codex]   │      → Session Gateway (:8081) ← OAuth2 → Auth0
[codex]   │           ├─ Permission Service (:8086) [email/displayName]
[codex]   │           └─ Redis (:6379) [session:*]
[codex]   ├─ /login, /* → NGINX (:8080) → budget-analyzer-web
[codex]   └─ /api/* → ext_authz HTTP service (:9002) → NGINX (:8080) → Backend Services
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Discovery**:
[codex] ```bash
[codex] # Find all Java source files
[codex] find src/main/java -name "*.java" | sort
[codex] 
[codex] # Find configuration classes
[codex] grep -r "class.*Config" src/main/java
[codex] 
[codex] # Check OAuth2 configuration
[codex] grep -r "oauth2" src/main/resources/
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Port Summary**:
[codex] - **443**: Istio Ingress Gateway (browser entry point, SSL termination, ext_authz integration)
[codex] - **8080**: NGINX Gateway (frontend and API routing)
[codex] - **8081**: Session Gateway (behind Istio ingress, receives auth/session lifecycle requests)
[codex] - **9002**: ext_authz HTTP service (called by the ingress Envoy proxy on `/api/*`)
[codex] - **8090**: ext_authz health endpoint
[codex] - **8086**: Permission Service (user roles and permissions)
[codex] - **6379**: Redis (session storage)
[codex] 
[codex] ## Technology Stack
[codex] 
[codex] **Principle**: Spring WebFlux reactive stack with OAuth2 and custom Redis session management.
[codex] 
[codex] **Discovery**:
[codex] ```bash
[codex] # View all dependencies
[codex] ./gradlew dependencies
[codex] 
[codex] # Check Spring Boot version
[codex] cat gradle/libs.versions.toml
[codex] 
[codex] # List key dependencies
[codex] grep "implementation" build.gradle.kts
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] **Stack Components**:
[codex] - **Web**: Spring WebFlux (reactive)
[codex] - **Security**: Spring Security OAuth2 Client
[codex] - **Sessions**: Custom Redis hash sessions via `SessionWriter`/`SessionReader` (not Spring Session)
[codex] - **Service Common (service-web)**: Reactive HTTP logging, correlation IDs, safe logging, exception handling
[codex] - **Permission Client**: WebClient for reactive HTTP calls to permission-service
[codex] - **Build**: Gradle with Kotlin DSL
[codex] - **Cache**: Redis (AOF persistence)
[codex] - **Identity Provider**: Auth0 (OAuth2/OIDC)
[codex] 
[codex] **Service-Common Integration**:
[codex] - Auto-configured reactive utilities from `org.budgetanalyzer:service-web:&lt;service-common-version>`
[codex] - Provides: HTTP request/response logging, distributed tracing correlation IDs, safe logging with sensitive data masking, global exception handling
[codex] - OAuth2ResourceServerSecurityConfig explicitly excluded (Session Gateway is OAuth2 Client, not Resource Server)
[codex] - DataSource/JPA auto-configuration excluded (no database required)
[codex]

[codex] ## Resolved reactive dependency graph
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,
[codex] weekly, and by manual dispatch. The job runs only for the `main` ref and uses
[codex] the official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` action with the open-source
[codex] `basic` cache provider. It resolves all projects and all resolvable
[codex] configurations so application, runtime, build, and test dependency trees are
[codex] included. Do not add configuration filters without proving equivalent coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Remote resolution uses `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_USERNAME` and
[codex] `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN`, exposed to Gradle as `GITHUB_ACTOR` and
[codex] `GITHUB_TOKEN`. These package-read credentials are distinct from
[codex] `${{ github.token }}`, which the action uses to submit the graph with the job's
[codex] only elevated permission, `contents: write`. The snapshot is submitted directly
[codex] and is not retained as an artifact or published as a Build Scan.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow must fail when package credentials are missing, either declared
[codex] `service-common` artifact cannot be read, dependency resolution is incomplete,
[codex] or GitHub rejects submission. Do not substitute Maven Local, omit the internal
[codex] dependencies, filter failed configurations, or treat graph-generation failure
[codex] as a clean security result. A build step resolves and verifies the application
[codex] and test trees before the official action performs its unfiltered graph pass;
[codex] this prevents the graph task's zero exit status from masking unresolved
[codex] configurations.
[codex] 
[codex] The accepted hosted graph must demonstrate the service's actual reactive tree,
[codex] including Spring WebFlux, Reactor Core, Reactor Netty, Netty, Spring Security,
[codex] Spring Framework, and Jackson where resolved in application runtime or test
[codex] configurations. Inspect Lettuce's Netty path as well as WebFlux's HTTP client and
[codex] server path. Embedded Tomcat is not an expected dependency for this reactive
[codex] service and must not be added as an artificial acceptance condition.
[codex] 
[codex] The credential-free Phase 7 run generated an official local plugin snapshot,
[codex] but it is deliberately recorded as incomplete. It contained 87 build/tool
[codex] coordinates and zero `org.budgetanalyzer`, Spring WebFlux, Spring Security,
[codex] Reactor, Reactor Netty, Netty, or Lettuce coordinates. Its only Spring
[codex] coordinates were `spring-core` and `spring-jcl`, alongside build-plugin Jackson
[codex] coordinates. Gradle's `runtimeClasspath` report marked every application
[codex] dependency failed, and
[codex] `./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency org.budgetanalyzer:service-web
[codex] --configuration runtimeClasspath` identified HTTP 401 from GitHub Packages for
[codex] `service-web` 0.0.16. No Netty coverage is available from that partial snapshot.
[codex] This is authentication-dependent local evidence, not a submitted graph or a
[codex] claim that those dependencies are absent.
