[codex] ## Implementation Guardrails
[codex] 
[codex] ### Architecture and API boundaries
[codex] 
[codex] - Keep feature code under `src/features/`; features must not import from other
[codex]   features. Put shared code in the appropriate top-level `src/` directory.
[codex] - Use the `@/*` alias instead of relative source imports.
[codex] - Components use TanStack Query hooks and mutation callbacks; they do not call
[codex]   Axios directly or copy server data into Redux.
[codex] - Match generated OpenAPI constraints in forms and keep
[codex]   `src/utils/errorMessages.ts` synchronized with backend application codes.
[codex] - Access the local application through
[codex]   `https://app.budgetanalyzer.localhost`, not the Vite port.
[codex] 
[codex] ### React and components
[codex] 
[codex] Read the [hooks guide](docs/react-hooks-lifecycle-mental-model.md) before
[codex] changing hooks or lifecycle behavior.
[codex] 
[codex] - Use effects only to synchronize external systems such as DOM APIs, timers,
[codex]   listeners, subscriptions, and imperative libraries. Clean up installed or
[codex]   acquired resources.
[codex] - Derive values during render, run user-driven work in event handlers, and use
[codex]   TanStack Query for server state.
[codex] - Keep components synchronous. Use `mutate(data, { onSuccess, onError })`
[codex]   instead of `mutateAsync` with component-level `async`/`await`.
[codex] - Memoize functions passed as props with `useCallback`.
[codex] - Do not put IIFEs, multi-line logic, or inline function definitions in JSX
[codex]   props; extract named callbacks or helpers.
[codex] - Never disable an ESLint rule without permission.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Authorization
[codex] 
[codex] - Roles choose layout chrome; never use `isAdmin` to gate an action.
[codex] - Permissions gate actions and feature access. Use `PermissionGuard` for a
[codex]   route or subtree and `usePermission` for an individual affordance.
[codex] - Denied `PermissionGuard` children must remain unmounted so their queries do
[codex]   not run.
[codex] - Use unscoped transaction permissions for a user's own data and `:any` only
[codex]   for distinct cross-user features.
[codex] - Call `usePermission` only at hook-safe top-level sites, never inside a filter,
[codex]   loop, or callback.
[codex] 
[codex] The [authentication owner](docs/authentication.md#roles-and-permissions)
[codex] contains the complete taxonomy and gating guidance.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Centralized conventions
[codex] 
[codex] - Define reusable animations in `src/lib/animations.ts`.
[codex] - Import date behavior only through `src/utils/dates.ts`, never directly from
[codex]   `date-fns`. LocalDate values have no timezone; ISO 8601 values do.
[codex] - Add dynamic table width mappings to `src/utils/columnWidth.ts`; never use a
[codex]   React `style` prop.
[codex] - Do not add transient toasts or a toast dependency. Keep actionable feedback
[codex]   persistent and contextual; informative cross-route results may use the
[codex]   existing flash-banner pattern. Follow the contract in
[codex]   [API integration](docs/api-integration.md#user-facing-error-messages).
[codex] - Shared `src/components/ui/Table.tsx` owns horizontal overflow. Feature tables
[codex]   must not hide its native scrollbar.
[codex] - Do not add tooltips; information must remain available on mobile.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Strict CSP
[codex] 
[codex] Application code must comply with `style-src 'self'` without `unsafe-inline` or
[codex] `unsafe-eval` and with the repository's stricter Tailwind-first conventions.
[codex] 
[codex] - Never add React `style={...}` props.
[codex] - Never add application code or dependencies that create runtime `&lt;style>`
[codex]   elements, insert CSSOM rules, write stylesheet content, or generate CSS with
[codex]   `eval()` or `new Function()`.
[codex] - Use `acquireBodyScrollLock()` from `src/utils/bodyScrollLock.ts` for overlay
[codex]   scroll locks.
[codex] - Treat bundle matches as capabilities to investigate, not as an allowlist or
[codex]   proof of execution. A serialized DOM `style` attribute alone is not proof of
[codex]   a browser CSP violation.
[codex] - Before adding a UI dependency, changing Motion usage or versions, or changing
[codex]   overlays, follow the static-scan and browser-audit requirements in
[codex]   [Architecture](docs/architecture.md#content-security-policy),
[codex]   [Development](docs/development.md#production-smoke-build-and-dropdown-gate),
[codex]   and [Testing](docs/testing-guide.md#external-browser-harness).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Testing
[codex] 
[codex] - Put production-code tests beside their owner in `__tests__/`; reserve
[codex]   `src/testing/` for shared infrastructure.
[codex] - Add a meaningful test for new behavior or explain explicitly why none is
[codex]   needed.
[codex] - Use MSW for new API-facing behavior unless a direct module mock is
[codex]   intentionally narrower.
[codex] - Prefer `@testing-library/user-event` for workflows and `fireEvent` only for
[codex]   low-level synthetic events.
[codex] - Test product behavior, not native browser, React, TypeScript, or third-party
[codex]   library behavior.
[codex] - Changes to `playwright.config.ts` or `e2e/` require
[codex]   `npm run typecheck:e2e`. Browser tests require the user-managed environment;
[codex]   agents must not start Tilt or Vite.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Working Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - Never run `npm run dev`; the user controls the development server.
[codex] - Use `npm run lint:fix`, not `npm run lint`, for agent validation.
[codex] - Never perform git write operations such as commit, push, checkout, or reset
[codex]   without an explicit user request. The user controls git operations.
[codex]

[codex]   build, and test behavior are unchanged.

[codex]   while iterating, and `npm run build` before handoff. The build includes the
[codex]   full coverage, TypeScript, and bundle gates.
[codex] - Test-only changes: run `npm run lint:fix` and the affected tests. Run
[codex]   `npm run test:coverage` when changing shared test infrastructure, coverage
[codex]   configuration, or behavior exercised across features.
[codex] - Changes to `playwright.config.ts` or `e2e/`: run `npm run lint:fix` and
[codex]   `npm run typecheck:e2e`. Run browser tests only when the user-managed
[codex]   environment is available and the Testing guide requires them.
[codex] - UI dependency, Motion, overlay, or CSP-sensitive changes: also run the static
[codex]   scan and browser-audit gates required by the Strict CSP section.
[codex] - Dependency-automation configuration or workflow changes: format changed

[codex] `renovate.json` extends the Budget Analyzer shared preset. Renovate discovers:
[codex]

[codex]   `package-lock.json`;

[codex] Routine updates and lockfile maintenance run on the shared weekly schedule.
[codex] React and React DOM updates are grouped, as are the Vitest runner, UI, and
[codex] coverage packages. The shared policy disables automerge, keeps patch, minor,
[codex] and major proposals distinguishable, and requires Dependency Dashboard approval
[codex] for majors. Toolchain majors such as TypeScript, Vite, Vitest, ESLint, Tailwind,
[codex] React Router, and Node therefore remain visible for compatibility review rather
[codex] than being excluded or constrained to historical target versions.

[codex] silently refresh the checked-in lockfile during onboarding. Review dependency
[codex] and lockfile diffs together. For image updates, retain immutable digests and
[codex] verify the selected tag/digest supports the required platform before merging.

[codex] ## Audit evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml` runs weekly and on manual dispatch. It
[codex] installs exactly `package-lock.json` with `npm ci`, then independently captures:
[codex] 
[codex] - `npm audit --json` as `npm-audit-full.json`;
[codex] - `npm audit --omit=dev --json` as `npm-audit-production.json`.
[codex] 
[codex] Download the `npm-audit-reports` artifact from the workflow run to compare the
[codex] raw JSON reports. The artifact is retained for seven days and also includes each
[codex] command's stderr and `status.txt`. The job summary presents severity counts for
[codex] the two scopes.
[codex] 
[codex] An npm audit exit status caused by findings does not fail this scheduled report;
[codex] the existing backlog remains visible without blocking unrelated pull requests.
[codex] Missing or malformed JSON, an npm-reported registry error, an unexpected command
[codex] status, or an `npm ci` failure does fail the workflow. Installation errors remain
[codex] separate in the named install step's log, while audit errors and partial report
[codex] files remain available through the always-upload artifact step.
[codex]

[codex] ## Reachable vulnerability evidence
[codex]

[codex] on manual dispatch. It installs the pinned official `govulncheck` CLI and runs
[codex] both `govulncheck ./...` and `govulncheck -json ./...`. The workflow keeps the
[codex] readable report, JSON event stream, stderr, scanner version, and exit-code summary
[codex] for seven days.
[codex] 
[codex] Reachable findings are reported and uploaded without failing unrelated work.
[codex] Scanner installation, package loading, vulnerability database access, analysis,
[codex] JSON generation or validation, empty required evidence, and artifact upload
[codex] failures still fail the job. In particular, the text command's exit code 3 means
[codex] findings, while any other unexpected text status or any nonzero JSON status is an
[codex] operational error.
[codex] 
[codex] The application still declares Go 1.24. The current pinned scanner,
[codex] `golang.org/x/vuln` v1.7.0, requires Go 1.25 or newer, so this workflow uses Go
[codex] 1.26.x solely as its analysis toolchain and sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` to prevent an
[codex] implicit toolchain change. That does not upgrade the application toolchain or its
[codex] builder image.

[codex] - Never use HTTP, `--insecure`, `verify=False`, or `ignore_https_errors` to bypass a local trust failure. Do not run the lazy trust command for staging, production, arbitrary origins, or non-certificate failures.

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared
[codex] [Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] remains alert-only.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] URLs:
[codex] 
[codex] | Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] | `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] | `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] | Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] 
[codex] Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] 
[codex] The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] checksum check.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] 
[codex] The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] 
[codex] A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] `Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] `FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Workspace image evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex]    registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex]    children.
[codex] 2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex]    without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] 3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex]    vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex]    Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex]    the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex]    binary.
[codex] 4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex]    for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] 
[codex] Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] never started.
[codex] 
[codex] The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] docker buildx build \
[codex]   --no-cache \
[codex]   --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex]   --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex]   --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex]   --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex]   --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex]   --load \
[codex]   ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] `ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Inventory limits
[codex] 
[codex] Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] `zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] 
[codex] The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] 
[codex] The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] `TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local baseline evidence
[codex] 
[codex] On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] `11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] 
[codex] The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both

[codex] image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] `24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local

[codex] scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go

[codex] or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the

[codex] 
[codex] A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records

[codex] ```

[codex] ## Core Product Constraints

[codex] ## Python Baseline
[codex] 
[codex] Use modern, explicit Python. The implementation should feel like a small typed
[codex] system, not loose scripting glue.
[codex] 
[codex] - Require Python 3.12 unless the project intentionally changes runtime support.
[codex] - Use a `src/` layout for importable code.
[codex] - Put tests outside application code under `tests/`.
[codex] - Configure packaging, Ruff, mypy, and pytest in `pyproject.toml`.
[codex] - Keep development dependencies separate from test-runner execution
[codex]   dependencies.
[codex] - Prefer standard-library types and modules for orchestration unless the
[codex]   repository plan explicitly calls for a test-harness dependency.
[codex] - Use `pathlib.Path` for filesystem paths.
[codex] - Read and write text with explicit `encoding="utf-8"`.
[codex] - Use timezone-aware UTC timestamps for generated ids and serialized state.
[codex] - Keep business logic out of CLI/tool entrypoints. Tools should parse
[codex]   arguments, call typed functions, print user-facing messages, and return exit
[codex]   codes.
[codex] - Implement tool entrypoints as `main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int`
[codex]   where practical.
[codex] - Keep generated artifacts out of version control: `.venv/`, `.mypy_cache/`,
[codex]   `.ruff_cache/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `*.egg-info/`, `__pycache__/`,
[codex]   `.coverage`, `htmlcov/`, `.pytest_cache/`, and generated request or coverage
[codex]   artifacts.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Typing Standards
[codex] 
[codex] - Run mypy in strict mode.
[codex] - Annotate all public functions, methods, dataclasses, and module-level
[codex]   constants where the type is not obvious.
[codex] - Prefer precise stdlib types from `collections.abc` such as `Sequence`,
[codex]   `Mapping`, `Iterable`, and `Callable` for interfaces.
[codex] - Avoid `Any`. If it is unavoidable at external boundaries such as decoded
[codex]   YAML, decoded JSON, OpenAPI documents, httpx, Playwright, or pytest hooks,
[codex]   isolate it and validate into typed dataclasses or Pydantic models quickly.
[codex] - Avoid broad `dict[str, object]` plumbing across modules.
[codex] - Use dataclasses or Pydantic models for durable value objects such as
[codex]   environment config, identities, run state, operation coverage, and process or
[codex]   request results.
[codex] - Use literals or enums for constrained status values, auth modes, environment
[codex]   types, cleanup modes, and coverage states.
[codex] - Do not silence mypy with broad ignore comments. A narrow ignore must include
[codex]   the error code and a short reason.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Formatting And Linting
[codex] 
[codex] Use Ruff as the single formatting, linting, pyupgrade, and import-sorting path.
[codex] Do not add Black, isort, Flake8, or autopep8 unless the user explicitly asks
[codex] for that tool split.
[codex] 
[codex] Expected commands in this workspace use the repository-local virtualenv. If
[codex] `.venv/` is missing, create or install the dev environment first rather than
[codex] falling back to global tooling.
[codex] 
[codex] Current transitional commands:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] .venv/bin/python -m ruff format .
[codex] .venv/bin/python -m ruff check . --fix
[codex] .venv/bin/python -m mypy src tests
[codex] .venv/bin/python -m pytest --env local --collect-only
[codex] .venv/bin/python tools/check-openapi-coverage.py --env local --fail-missing --fail-placeholder
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] After the `src/` migration, the mypy command should be:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] .venv/bin/python -m mypy src tests
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Ruff should use `line-length = 100`, `target-version = "py312"`,
[codex] `src = ["src", "tests"]`, and lint selections including `E`, `F`, `I`, `UP`,
[codex] `B`, `SIM`, and `RUF`.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Testing Standards
[codex] 
[codex] Use pytest for tests.
[codex] 
[codex] - Prefer `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`, `capsys`, `httpx.MockTransport`, and
[codex]   `respx` for harness unit tests.
[codex] - Do not call real identity providers or live Budget Analyzer targets from unit
[codex]   tests.
[codex] - Keep tests deterministic. Avoid sleeps except where timeout behavior is under
[codex]   test, and keep those durations short.
[codex] - Use OpenAPI markers consistently:
[codex] 
[codex]   ```python
[codex]   @pytest.mark.openapi("operationId")
[codex]   ```
[codex] 
[codex] - Use `placeholder` only while a phase is under construction. Placeholder
[codex]   coverage is not an acceptable staging-gate completion state.
[codex] - Mark mutating tests with `mutation`, destructive tests with `destructive`,
[codex]   read-only tests with `readonly`, authorization tests with `authorization`,
[codex]   and production-safe tests with `production_safe`.
[codex] - Production execution should select only explicitly production-safe read-only
[codex]   tests.
[codex] - Mutation and destructive markers must be blocked by environment policy before
[codex]   request fixtures or network-capable clients are set up.
[codex] - For pytest configuration, prefer strict config, strict markers, declared test
[codex]   paths, and importlib import mode.
[codex] 
[codex] ## API Execution Safety
[codex] 
[codex] - Use `GatewayClient` for API requests so base origin, API prefix, TLS policy,
[codex]   timeout, cookies, and request logging stay centralized.
[codex] - Preserve HTTPS certificate verification for live tests in every environment,
[codex]   including local Tilt targets. Do not add insecure runner flags, environment
[codex]   switches, `verify=False`, Playwright `ignore_https_errors`, or equivalent
[codex]   bypasses for agent containers.
[codex] - Treat a missing host CA in an agent container as a runner trust-store
[codex]   prerequisite. Make the host-generated public mkcert CA certificate available
[codex]   to the container and configure its Python and browser trust stores instead of
[codex]   weakening TLS verification.
[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared
[codex] [Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] remains alert-only.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. This repository is PEP
[codex] 621, not Poetry, so its configuration disables Renovate's Poetry manager to
[codex] prevent that manager from superseding the native PEP 621 manager. The PEP 621
[codex] manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and the GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] 
[codex] The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] 
[codex] - `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex]   ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex]   does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] - Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex]   checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex]   requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] - The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex]   concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] `.[dev]`, and records both JSON and line-oriented installed-version lists using
[codex] `pip list`. This avoids writing the editable checkout URL into the artifact.
[codex] The lists include runtime and development dependencies, but the workflow
[codex] deliberately does not install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests
[codex] against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] 
[codex] The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] 
[codex] The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] pull requests.
[codex] 
[codex] The audit covers packages retained in the installed test environment. The
[codex] isolated build environment used temporarily for `setuptools>=69` is not part of
[codex] that installed set; Renovate extraction and hosted dependency-graph evidence are
[codex] the update and advisory paths for that build requirement.
[codex]

[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,

[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared Budget Analyzer preset. Renovate's native
[codex] Gradle, Gradle Wrapper, Dockerfile, and GitHub Actions managers discover this
[codex] repository's version catalog, build script, wrapper distribution, base images,
[codex] and workflow actions. The Gradle catalog extraction includes the declared
[codex] `serviceCommon` version used by `spring-platform` and `service-web`.
[codex]

[codex] Renovate can look up those private Maven coordinates. Before activation,
[codex] configure the Mend Renovate Community App's supported encrypted Maven
[codex] credentials and verify an authenticated lookup; never put a package token in
[codex] this repository or the shared preset. The app must keep direct,
[codex] maintained-line, and later-major proposals visible where each datasource
[codex] supports them.
[codex] 
[codex] The Phase 5 local extraction found 45 dependency occurrences across eight
[codex] files: 25 Gradle occurrences in three files, one wrapper occurrence, three
[codex] Dockerfile occurrences, and 16 GitHub Actions occurrences in three workflows.
[codex] Public Gradle, wrapper, and image lookups produced 45 candidate branches at the
[codex] time of validation. GitHub Actions lookups and the three
[codex] `org.budgetanalyzer` Maven catalog coordinates remain authenticated hosted
[codex] checks; the local runner had no GitHub or package-read token, so those checks
[codex] are pending rather than passed.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate proposes changes only to direct declarations. Versions inherited from
[codex] the Spring Boot and `spring-platform` BOMs remain represented by the resolved
[codex] dependency graph described below. A direct Spring Boot or `serviceCommon`
[codex] proposal is not proof that every inherited vulnerability is fixed.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Resolved dependency graph
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-submission.yml` runs on trusted pushes to `main`,
[codex] weekly, and by manual dispatch. The job runs only for the `main` ref and uses
[codex] the official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` action with the open-source
[codex] `basic` cache provider. It resolves all projects and all resolvable
[codex] configurations so application, runtime, build, and test dependency trees are
[codex] included. Do not add configuration filters without proving equivalent
[codex] coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Remote resolution uses `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_USERNAME` and
[codex] `SERVICE_COMMON_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN`, exposed to Gradle as `GITHUB_ACTOR` and
[codex] `GITHUB_TOKEN`. These package-read credentials are distinct from
[codex] `${{ github.token }}`, which the action uses to submit the graph with the job's
[codex] only elevated permission, `contents: write`. The package-access preflight
[codex] checks the exact `spring-platform` and `service-web` artifacts used by this
[codex] service. The snapshot is submitted directly and is not retained as an artifact
[codex] or published as a Build Scan.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow must fail when package credentials are missing, either pinned
[codex] `service-common` artifact cannot be resolved, graph generation is incomplete,
[codex] or GitHub rejects submission. Do not substitute Maven Local, omit an internal
[codex] dependency, filter failed configurations, or treat graph-generation failure as
[codex] a clean security result. A hosted run on `main` is the final proof that GitHub
[codex] accepted the submission and can produce Dependabot alerts from it.
[codex] 
[codex] Local Phase 5 validation ran the official GitHub dependency graph Gradle plugin
[codex] without submitting its output. The generated snapshot contained 87 build/tool
[codex] coordinates and eight direct entries, but no `org.budgetanalyzer`, Spring
[codex] Security, Tomcat, Netty, PostgreSQL, Testcontainers, or WireMock coordinates.
[codex] The accompanying `runtimeClasspath` report marked `spring-platform`,
[codex] `service-web`, and every dependent application runtime declaration as failed to
[codex] resolve because the credential-free environment could not access the pinned
[codex] private artifacts. This partial snapshot proves only that local generation ran;
[codex] it is not application, runtime, test, remote-resolution, or submission evidence.
[codex]

[codex] updates remain visible in the Dependency Dashboard and require approval.
[codex]

[codex]

[codex] ./gradlew clean build
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Bot pull requests use the existing `build.yml` pull-request workflow. Forked or
[codex] otherwise untrusted pull requests do not receive package-read secrets, so a
[codex] failure to resolve `service-common` there is an unavailable-secret condition,
[codex] not evidence that the dependency is absent. Do not add `pull_request_target` or
[codex] expose package credentials to untrusted dependency branches to bypass that
[codex] boundary.

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared
[codex] [Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] remains alert-only.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] URLs:
[codex] 
[codex] | Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] | `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] | `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] | Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] | Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] 
[codex] Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] 
[codex] The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] checksum check.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] 
[codex] The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] 
[codex] A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] `Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] `FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Workspace image evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex]    registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex]    children.
[codex] 2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex]    without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] 3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex]    vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex]    Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex]    the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex]    binary.
[codex] 4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex]    for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] 
[codex] Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] never started.
[codex] 
[codex] The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] docker buildx build \
[codex]   --no-cache \
[codex]   --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex]   --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex]   --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex]   --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex]   --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex]   --load \
[codex]   ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] `ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Inventory limits
[codex] 
[codex] Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] `zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] 
[codex] Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] 
[codex] The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] 
[codex] The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] `TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex]

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow are prepared; automation is
[codex] not installed or active. Hosted acceptance remains pending Phase 12.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared
[codex] [Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] remains alert-only.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. This repository is PEP
[codex] 621, not Poetry, so its configuration disables Renovate's Poetry manager to
[codex] prevent that manager from superseding the native PEP 621 manager. The PEP 621
[codex] manager reads `pyproject.toml`, and the GitHub Actions manager reads
[codex] `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml`. A repository regex manager
[codex] tracks the workflow's exact `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION` as the `pip-audit` PyPI package.
[codex] The shared preset must be published before activating this consumer.
[codex] 
[codex] The Python declarations intentionally retain their existing constraint policy:
[codex] 
[codex] - `setuptools>=69` and `requires-python = ">=3.12"` are lower bounds whose
[codex]   ranges already admit later compatible versions. Renovate can extract them but
[codex]   does not need to raise a lower bound merely because a newer release exists.
[codex] - Runtime and development requirements are unbounded package names. They have no
[codex]   checked-in current version for Renovate to update, so routine version pull
[codex]   requests are not expected for those declarations.
[codex] - The exact `pip-audit` workflow version and versioned GitHub Actions do provide
[codex]   concrete current values and can receive update proposals.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not add upper bounds, exact application dependency pins, or a lockfile solely
[codex] to manufacture Renovate pull requests. Reinstalling `.[dev]` selects whatever
[codex] versions satisfy the declarations at that time. It does not reconstruct a
[codex] historical environment and is not reproducible evidence of an earlier run.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Installed-environment audit evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/python-dependency-audit.yml` runs every Monday and by manual
[codex] dispatch. It creates a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment, installs
[codex] `.[dev]`, and records both JSON and line-oriented installed-version lists using
[codex] `pip list`. This avoids writing the editable checkout URL into the artifact.
[codex] The lists include runtime and development dependencies, but the workflow
[codex] deliberately does not install Playwright browser binaries or run any tests
[codex] against Budget Analyzer.
[codex] 
[codex] The first-party editable package has no PyPI advisory identity. After dependency
[codex] installation and full version capture, the workflow removes only its editable
[codex] metadata and uses pinned `pip-audit` 2.10.1 from a separate scanner environment
[codex] to audit the remaining installed third-party package set. Strict mode, an exact
[codex] comparison between installed and reported names and versions, and JSON shape
[codex] checks prevent a partial result from being treated as complete.
[codex] 
[codex] The `python-dependency-audit-&lt;commit>` artifact is retained for seven days and
[codex] contains the standard `pip-audit` JSON report, stderr, exit code, scanner and
[codex] Python versions, installed package lists, install logs, and a summary. Finding
[codex] exit status 1 is accepted only when the complete JSON report contains findings.
[codex] Missing or malformed output, dependency collection gaps, version mismatches,
[codex] installation or advisory-service errors, and unexpected exit statuses fail the
[codex] workflow. Findings remain visible without creating a merge gate for unrelated
[codex] pull requests.
[codex] 
[codex] The audit covers packages retained in the installed test environment. The
[codex] isolated build environment used temporarily for `setuptools>=69` is not part of
[codex] that installed set; Renovate extraction and hosted dependency-graph evidence are
[codex] the update and advisory paths for that build requirement.
[codex]

[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access through the Phase 12 operator handoff. During Phases 1–11,
[codex]   record authentication-dependent checks as pending and continue independent local
[codex]   work. Never seek credentials in the agent environment, use Maven Local as proof
[codex]   of remote resolution, drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error. A
[codex]   resolution defect unrelated to authentication still needs investigation.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.
[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] 
[codex] This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] [September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] [dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership and policy
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared policy is
[codex] [`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] 
[codex] Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] or upstream support status.
[codex] 
[codex] The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] 
[codex] - historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] - local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex]   inventories
[codex] - first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex]   overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] - Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] - arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cost and service boundary
[codex] 
[codex] Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] `govulncheck`.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Activation procedure
[codex] 
[codex] Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] prepared and locally validated their files. Phases 1–11 require no credentials;
[codex] all authenticated validation and credential review belong to Phase 12. Agents
[codex] must never receive GitHub, package, registry, or Mend credentials, including in
[codex] Phase 12. The user performs authenticated operations in GitHub/Mend or their own
[codex] trusted environment and supplies sanitized evidence for agent review.
[codex] 
[codex] Missing authentication, authenticated-only API access, and unauthenticated API
[codex] rate limits are recorded as pending Phase 12 evidence; they do not block local
[codex] configuration preparation. This includes private Maven resolution, complete
[codex] remotely resolved Java snapshots, graph submission, published-preset resolution,
[codex] and hosted bot/scanner runs. Local schema validation, extraction, workflow lint,
[codex] and checks that can run without credentials remain required. Preserve actual
[codex] failures and incomplete outputs; never report a deferred check as passed or
[codex] weaken a hosted job's failure behavior. Non-authentication prerequisites and
[codex] implementation defects remain blockers under the owning repository's rules.
[codex] 
[codex] For each deferred check, record the repository, check/command, affected packages
[codex] or configurations, observed failure or reason not attempted, and the Phase 12
[codex] operator action and expected proof. Sibling phases keep this handoff in their
[codex] own docs and link here; Phase 12 consolidates it in the coverage report.
[codex] 
[codex] The Phase 12 operator sequence is:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex]    free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex]    Maven lookup within its job limits. Complete this before publication can
[codex]    trigger any prepared push workflows.
[codex] 2. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex]    consumer configurations.
[codex] 3. Manually dispatch
[codex]    `dependency-automation-config.yml` with `run_hosted_dry_run` enabled. Its
[codex]    GitHub-provided job token has read permissions only, Renovate runs with
[codex]    `--dry-run=full`, and the user retains control of the trigger. Preserve the
[codex]    workflow URL and confirm that the published preset resolves before proceeding;
[codex]    never copy the job token into an agent environment.
[codex] 4. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex]    rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] 5. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex]    updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] 6. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex]    and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex]    expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] 7. Run each Java repository's graph-submission workflow on its trusted default
[codex]    branch using its existing scoped package-read secrets and a separate GitHub
[codex]    job token for submission. Verify complete application/runtime/test dependency
[codex]    coverage and GitHub acceptance for every repo. A successful ordinary build,
[codex]    package-access preflight, or partial snapshot is insufficient. Preserve a
[codex]    sanitized snapshot or equivalent detailed graph evidence with the run URL and
[codex]    source revision; the orchestration-only Renovate dry run does not prove Maven
[codex]    resolution or Java submission. Resolve every other deferred authenticated
[codex]    lookup/build/scan and retain its evidence too.
[codex] 8. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex]    extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex]    message before enabling consumers.
[codex] 9. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex]    false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex]    and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] 
[codex] The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.

[codex] ## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] 
[codex] Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] 
[codex] - the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] - the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] - a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] - a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] - Trivy CLI/database and registry-resolver metadata, database-download logs,
[codex]   and a machine-readable completion status
[codex] 
[codex] A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] 23:extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] 45:Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] 120:   extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex] 150:`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] 195:target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] 205:## Failure triage
[codex] 214:  unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.

[codex] # Dependency Update Review Baseline
[codex] 
[codex] **Date:** 2026-09-06  
[codex] **Status:** Point-in-time research  
[codex] **Purpose:** Preserve the manually researched dependency recommendations so
[codex] they can be compared with repository-owned Dependabot and Renovate findings
[codex] after that automation is enabled.
[codex] 
[codex] This is not a version contract or an implementation plan. Upstream current
[codex] versions will continue to change. Checked-in build files, manifests, version
[codex] catalogs, and `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh` remain the sources of
[codex] truth for selected versions.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Executive Summary
[codex] 
[codex] The highest-priority work is not a blanket migration to every current major.
[codex] It is a security patch batch covering Redis, the Spring-managed dependency
[codex] stack, External Secrets Operator, Kyverno, the frontend dependency tree,
[codex] `go-redis`, the JDK runtime image, and selected observability components.
[codex] 
[codex] Several runtime lines are also unsupported or approaching end of support:
[codex] Spring Boot 3.5, Node.js 20, Go 1.24, RabbitMQ 3.13, NGINX 1.29, and production
[codex] Kubernetes/K3s 1.34. Those should be handled as explicit migration batches
[codex] rather than mixed into low-risk security patch updates.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Security And Maintenance Patch Recommendations
[codex] 
[codex] ### Redis Server
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in reference | `redis:7-alpine@sha256:7aec734b...` |
[codex] | Version resolved from the digest | Redis 7.4.8, image created 2026-04-17 |
[codex] | Recommended supported-line patch | Redis 7.4.11 |
[codex] | Major migration status | Redis 8 exists, but is not required for support |
[codex] 
[codex] Redis 7.4.8 predates the May 2026 security release and is affected by multiple
[codex] authenticated memory-safety vulnerabilities, including a `RESTORE` command
[codex] issue that may lead to remote code execution. This has practical relevance to
[codex] the current ACL model: `session-gateway` and `redis-ops` receive `+@all`, while
[codex] the other service identities are substantially narrower.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: refresh the Redis 7.4 image to 7.4.11 before considering a
[codex] Redis 8 migration. Review whether `session-gateway` needs `+@all` or can use an
[codex] explicit command allowlist that excludes administrative commands such as
[codex] `RESTORE`.
[codex] 
[codex] Primary advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4](https://github.com/redis/redis/security/advisories/GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Spring Boot-Managed Backend Stack
[codex] 
[codex] The checked-in Spring Boot 3.5.14 BOM resolves these notable components:
[codex] 
[codex] | Component | Boot 3.5.14 | Boot 3.5.16 | Security floor observed in this review |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Spring Framework | 6.2.18 | 6.2.19 | 6.2.19 |
[codex] | Spring Security | 6.5.10 | 6.5.11 | No advisory found for 6.5.10 in the queried database |
[codex] | Jackson BOM | 2.21.2 | 2.21.4 | 2.21.4 |
[codex] | Netty | 4.1.132.Final | 4.1.135.Final | 4.1.137.Final |
[codex] | Embedded Tomcat | 10.1.54 | 10.1.55 | 10.1.58 |
[codex] 
[codex] Findings include:
[codex] 
[codex] - Spring Web 6.2.18 is affected by an `UriComponentsBuilder` SSRF advisory;
[codex]   6.2.19 contains the fix.
[codex] - Jackson 2.21.2 is affected by deserialization authorization and polymorphic
[codex]   type validation issues; the relevant 2.x fixes are present in 2.21.4.
[codex] - Netty 4.1.132 is affected by request-smuggling, decompression denial of
[codex]   service, CORS bypass, CRLF injection, and resource exhaustion advisories.
[codex] - Tomcat 10.1.54 is in the affected ranges for several authorization and
[codex]   authentication advisories. The newest reviewed fixes require 10.1.58.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: first move the coordinated Java repositories to Spring Boot
[codex] 3.5.16. Because its BOM still selects Netty 4.1.135 and Tomcat 10.1.55, assess
[codex] temporary managed-version overrides to Netty 4.1.137 and Tomcat 10.1.58. Keep
[codex] this patch batch separate from the Spring Boot 4 migration.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveat: several Tomcat findings concern container-managed
[codex] FORM/DIGEST authentication, WebDAV, AJP, or direct HTTP/2 behavior that the
[codex] current services do not appear to use. The affected components are still in
[codex] the deployed classpath, so patching remains preferable to relying only on
[codex] configuration non-use. Netty is directly relevant to the reactive Session
[codex] Gateway and other WebFlux/WebClient paths.
[codex] 
[codex] Representative advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [Spring Framework SSRF](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7m2p-62gw-p8qq)
[codex] - [Tomcat security constraint bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5m62-pw8w-7w9f)
[codex] - [Tomcat authentication bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9xv2-5v5q-p794)
[codex] - [Netty request smuggling](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-38f8-5428-x5cv)
[codex] - [Netty CORS header issue](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8c42-7qj2-3j46)
[codex] - [Jackson polymorphic validation bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm)
[codex] 
[codex] ### External Secrets Operator
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart | 2.2.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | 2.4.0 |
[codex] | Current chart at review time | 2.10.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] External Secrets 2.2.0 is affected by DNS-based secret exfiltration through
[codex] the v2 template engine and a namespace-isolation bypass in `CAProvider`
[codex] ConfigMap resolution. Because this controller handles production secrets and
[codex] has broad cluster authority, it belongs in the critical monitoring tier even
[codex] though it was omitted from the former notification guide.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: validate a direct move to the current 2.10.0 chart. Do not
[codex] remain below 2.4.0.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3)
[codex] - [GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59)
[codex] 
[codex] ### Kyverno
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart/application | 3.8.0 / 1.18.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | Application 1.18.2 |
[codex] | Current chart/application at review time | 3.9.0 / 1.19.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] Kyverno 1.18.0 and 1.18.1 are affected by a critical cross-namespace resource
[codex] generation vulnerability in namespaced CEL policies. The current repository
[codex] does not define `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` or `NamespacedGeneratingPolicy`
[codex] resources, which reduces present exploitability, but the controller is a
[codex] privileged admission component.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: update the Helm chart and Kyverno CLI together to the 1.19.0
[codex] application line, then render and rerun the existing policy and security
[codex] guardrail tests.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/security/advisories/GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Frontend Dependency Tree
[codex] 
[codex] `npm audit` against the checked-in lockfile reported 20 findings: 3 critical,
[codex] 13 high, 2 moderate, and 2 low. `npm audit --omit=dev` reported four high
[codex] findings associated with Axios, React Router, React Router DOM, and a
[codex] transitive Axios dependency.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommended patch batch:
[codex] 
[codex] | Package | Checked-in/locked baseline | Patch target at review time |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | React / React DOM | 19.2.5 | 19.2.8 |
[codex] | React Router / React Router DOM | 7.14.2 | 7.18.3 |
[codex] | Axios | 1.16.0 | 1.20.0 |
[codex] | Vite | 6.4.2 | 6.4.3 or a separately planned major |
[codex] | Vitest packages | 3.2.4 | 3.2.7 or a separately planned major |
[codex] | PostCSS | 8.5.14 | 8.5.28 |
[codex] 
[codex] Refresh the lockfile after updating the direct dependencies so patched
[codex] versions of `form-data`, `brace-expansion`, `browserslist`, `flatted`,
[codex] `js-yaml`, `nanoid`, `picomatch`, and `ws` are selected.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveats:
[codex] 
[codex] - The critical Vitest issue requires the Vitest UI server to be listening; it
[codex]   is a development-tool risk, not production browser code.
[codex] - The reviewed Vite 6.4.2 issue requires a network-exposed Windows dev server.
[codex]   The supported container path is Linux, but the patch is still low risk.
[codex] - Most React Router findings concern framework, SSR, manifest, or RSC modes.
[codex]   The application uses `BrowserRouter`, not those server modes. The open
[codex]   redirect advisory is the most relevant browser-side reason to update.
[codex] - React Server Component advisories do not apply because no
[codex]   `react-server-dom-*` package is installed. React 19.2.8 remains the sensible
[codex]   paired patch level.
[codex] 
[codex] ### ext-authz And go-redis
[codex] 
[codex] `govulncheck` found a reachable call path from `ext-authz` to GO-2025-3540 in
[codex] `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` 9.7.0. The issue may cause out-of-order responses
[codex] when `CLIENT SETINFO` times out during connection establishment. The first
[codex] fixed version is 9.7.3; the current release at review time is 9.22.0.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: update within go-redis v9, rerun `go mod tidy`, `go test ./...`,
[codex] `govulncheck ./...`, and the shared session-contract verifiers.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisory: [GO-2025-3540](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3540).
[codex] 
[codex] ### JDK Runtime Image
[codex] 
[codex] The pinned `eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine` digest resolves to JDK 25.0.3+9,
[codex] created on 2026-04-30. The current Temurin 25 maintenance release is
[codex] 25.0.4.1+1.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: refresh the Temurin digest and verify that the separately
[codex] installed Azul Zulu 25 devcontainer package receives the same quarterly CPU
[codex] level. Java 25 remains the selected LTS baseline; this is not a Java feature
[codex] release migration.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Istio
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in release | 1.29.2 |
[codex] | Latest patch on selected line | 1.29.7 |
[codex] | Current minor at review time | 1.31.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] Istio 1.29.2 is affected by a medium-severity failure mode in which an
[codex] unresolved `BackendTLSPolicy` CA reference can cause sidecars to send upstream
[codex] traffic in plaintext. The repository does not currently define a
[codex] `BackendTLSPolicy`, so the advisory is not presently reachable through the
[codex] checked-in configuration.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: take 1.29.7 as the minimum maintenance update and plan a move
[codex] to 1.30 or 1.31 with the Kubernetes, Gateway API, and Calico batch. Istio 1.29
[codex] is expected to leave support around the end of October 2026.
[codex] 
[codex] Sources:
[codex] 
[codex] - [Istio advisory GHSA-qm8v-g4f9-qhjx](https://github.com/istio/istio/security/advisories/GHSA-qm8v-g4f9-qhjx)
[codex] - [Istio supported releases](https://istio.io/latest/docs/releases/supported-releases/)
[codex] 
[codex] ### Observability
[codex] 
[codex] | Component | Checked-in version | Recommendation |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Prometheus | 3.11.1 | At least 3.11.3; prefer a currently supported line such as 3.13 |
[codex] | Grafana | 12.4.2 | Refresh to the latest 12.4 patch, 12.4.10 at review time |
[codex] | Prometheus Operator | 0.90.1 via chart 83.4.0 | Review through the chart upgrade |
[codex] | kube-prometheus-stack | 83.4.0 | Current chart was 89.2.2; treat as a rendered-manifest migration |
[codex] | Jaeger | 2.17.0 | Current was 2.20.0; no directly applicable advisory found |
[codex] | Kiali | 2.24.0 | Current chart was 2.31.0; no directly applicable advisory found |
[codex] 
[codex] Prometheus 3.11.1 is the last affected release for a stored XSS issue and is
[codex] also affected by a remote-read denial-of-service issue fixed in 3.11.3. The
[codex] observability services are internal-only and operator access is loopback-only,
[codex] which lowers exposure but does not eliminate the need for patching.
[codex] 
[codex] Sources:
[codex] 
[codex] - [Prometheus stored XSS](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vffh-x6r8-xx99)
[codex] - [Prometheus remote-read denial of service](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/security/advisories/GHSA-8rm2-7qqf-34qm)
[codex] 
[codex] ### PostgreSQL
[codex] 
[codex] The pinned `postgres:16-alpine` digest resolves to PostgreSQL 16.13. The
[codex] current patch at review time is 16.15.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: refresh to PostgreSQL 16.15 as routine security and bug-fix
[codex] maintenance. PostgreSQL 16 remains supported until November 2028, so the
[codex] existence of PostgreSQL 18 does not make a database major-version migration
[codex] urgent.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Unsupported Or Approaching-EOL Migration Batches
[codex] 
[codex] ### Spring 4 Migration
[codex] 
[codex] Spring Boot 3.5.16 was the latest 3.5 release found, and the standard 3.5
[codex] open-source lifecycle ended in June 2026. Current Spring releases at review
[codex] time were Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring Cloud 2025.1.3, and Spring Security 7.1.1.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: complete the Spring Boot 3.5 security patch batch first, then
[codex] plan the already identified coupled migration to Spring Boot 4, Spring Cloud
[codex] 2025.1, Spring Framework 7, Spring Security 7, Spring Modulith 2, SpringDoc 3,
[codex] Testcontainers 2, ShedLock 7, and JUnit Platform 6.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Node.js
[codex] 
[codex] The frontend Dockerfiles use Node 20, which reached end of life on 2026-04-30.
[codex] The devcontainer already selects Node 22 even though the orchestration docs
[codex] still say Node 20.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: move production and development frontend builds to Node 24
[codex] LTS. Do not target Node 26 until it enters LTS unless there is a deliberate
[codex] reason to follow the current feature line.
[codex] 
[codex] Source: [Node.js releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Go
[codex] 
[codex] Go 1.24 is outside the supported two-release window. Go 1.27.1 was current at
[codex] review time, with Go 1.26 also supported.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: choose Go 1.26 for the conservative baseline or Go 1.27 for
[codex] the current baseline, and update `ext-authz`, its builder image, and the
[codex] devcontainer together. The devcontainer download is also hardcoded to the
[codex] amd64 archive and should be made architecture-aware as part of that work.
[codex] 
[codex] Source: [Go release policy](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#policy).
[codex] 
[codex] ### RabbitMQ
[codex] 
[codex] The pinned digest resolves to RabbitMQ 3.13.7. RabbitMQ 3.13 has been out of
[codex] community support since September 2024; RabbitMQ 4.3.5 was current at review
[codex] time.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: create a dedicated stateful migration plan to RabbitMQ 4.3,
[codex] covering supported upgrade hops, feature flags, persisted data compatibility,
[codex] definitions import, Spring Cloud Stream compatibility, rollback, and backup
[codex] evidence.
[codex] 
[codex] Source: [RabbitMQ release information](https://www.rabbitmq.com/release-information).
[codex] 
[codex] ### NGINX
[codex] 
[codex] The edge gateway uses NGINX 1.29.4, and the 1.29 mainline is no longer
[codex] supported. NGINX 1.30.4 was the stable line and 1.31.5 the mainline release at
[codex] review time.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: select either stable 1.30.4 or mainline 1.31.5 and update the
[codex] unprivileged image, configuration validation, security documentation, and
[codex] routing smoke tests together.
[codex]
