[codex] ## Documentation Drift Found During The Review
[codex] 
[codex] The former dependency notification guide is unsuitable as the primary alert
[codex] mechanism, but it also contains concrete drift worth preserving before it is
[codex] archived:
[codex] 
[codex] - It says no known issues are tracked, which is no longer true.
[codex] - It omits K3s, External Secrets Operator, cert-manager, the Prometheus stack,
[codex]   Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, Kiali, Swagger UI, and other deployed images
[codex]   from its supposedly complete inventory.
[codex] - It records only human-readable image tags, hiding the exact patch version
[codex]   frozen behind each digest.
[codex] - It says Node 20 will reach EOL in April 2026; that date has passed.
[codex] - It treats Go 1.24 and RabbitMQ 3.13 as moderate-priority maintained lines;
[codex]   both are unsupported.
[codex] - It says Redis 7 is the current major and refers to PostgreSQL 17 as the next
[codex]   major; Redis 8 and PostgreSQL 18 are current.
[codex] - It says Helm 4 is only a future GA timeline to watch; Helm 4 is already GA.
[codex] - Its Istio support description uses an N/N-1 rule. Upstream currently defines
[codex]   support until approximately six weeks after N+2.
[codex] - Its Vite summary says 6.0.1 while the inventory and package manifest say
[codex]   6.4.2.
[codex] - It calls Motion "Framer Motion" 11.11.17 while the frontend now depends on
[codex]   the `motion` package at 13.1.0.
[codex] - `docs/development/devcontainer-installed-software.md` says Node 20 although
[codex]   the sibling Dockerfile selects Node 22, and says cert-manager 1.13.2 while
[codex]   the production version contract selects 1.20.2.
[codex] 
[codex] When dependency automation is implemented, update the canonical owner first,
[codex] then synchronize `docs/development/local-environment.md`,
[codex] `docs/development/devcontainer-installed-software.md`,
[codex] `docs/architecture/security-architecture.md`,
[codex] `docs/architecture/observability.md`, and `deploy/README.md` only where their
[codex] owned behavior or exact operational contract changes. Do not rewrite ADRs to
[codex] reflect current versions.

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.

[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex] ## Current outcome
[codex] 
[codex] Installation status and benchmark parity are both **not established**. Local
[codex] configuration and scanner preparation are complete, but automation is not
[codex] demonstrably active and no Phase 12 authenticated operational check has passed.
[codex] The operator evidence in the tables above is required before this report can
[codex] record two bot cycles, a scheduled scan cycle, accepted Java graphs, or final
[codex] benchmark dispositions. Existing local misses remain gaps; lifecycle and
[codex] exploitability assessment remain human work.
[codex] they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] still fail the job.
[codex] 
[codex] Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] package scan.

[codex] ## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] 
[codex] Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] verified operating history.
[codex] 
[codex] Every week, an operator should:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex]    pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex]    Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex]    migrations.
[codex] 2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex]    the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex]    update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] 3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex]    Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex]    inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex]    operation, not a clean result.
[codex] 4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex]    credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex]    trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex]    `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] 5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex]    first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex]    duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex]    boundary.
[codex] 
[codex] Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] detectors.
[codex] 
[codex] When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access through the Phase 12 operator handoff. During Phases 1–11,
[codex]   record authentication-dependent checks as pending and continue independent local
[codex]   work. Never seek credentials in the agent environment, use Maven Local as proof
[codex]   of remote resolution, drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error. A
[codex]   resolution defect unrelated to authentication still needs investigation.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Post-activation operator workflow
[codex] +
[codex] +Begin this routine only after Phase 12 records successful activation evidence
[codex] +in the coverage report. Until then, the same checks are acceptance work, not a
[codex] +verified operating history.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every week, an operator should:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Review each scoped repository's Dependency Dashboard, newly opened Renovate
[codex] +   pull requests, and any lookup, authentication, timeout, or rate-limit error.
[codex] +   Keep maintained-line patches visible alongside approval-gated majors and
[codex] +   migrations.
[codex] +2. Review Dependabot alerts separately from update proposals. Map each alert to
[codex] +   the resolved package and configuration or image artifact; never treat an
[codex] +   update pull request as proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] +3. Check the latest scheduled dependency-submission and scanner workflows.
[codex] +   Distinguish vulnerability findings from failed resolution, database download,
[codex] +   inventory, or report generation. A missing or partial report is a failed
[codex] +   operation, not a clean result.
[codex] +4. Review bot pull-request checks and any package/registry access failure. Keep
[codex] +   credentials in GitHub or Mend's supported encrypted storage and preserve the
[codex] +   trusted-branch boundary; never move dependency checks to
[codex] +   `pull_request_target` to expose secrets.
[codex] +5. Confirm Renovate remains the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains off,
[codex] +   first-party production promotion paths are untouched, and free-service job
[codex] +   duration/queueing plus Actions usage remain within the approved zero-spend
[codex] +   boundary.
[codex] +
[codex] +Every quarter, compare Spring, Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu, Kubernetes/K3s, Istio,
[codex] +RabbitMQ, NGINX, and other runtime lines with their upstream lifecycle policies.
[codex] +Record the review even when Renovate proposes no update: release discovery,
[codex] +abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability databases are not comprehensive EOL
[codex] +detectors.
[codex] +
[codex] +When adding a dependency, first use the owning ecosystem's native Renovate
[codex] +manager and confirm extraction in debug logs. If the version is embedded in a
[codex] +supported nonstandard declaration, add the smallest adjacent standard Renovate
[codex] +annotation or declarative regex manager in the owning repository. Preserve tag
[codex] +prefixes, flavor suffixes, immutable digests, checksums, chart coupling, and
[codex] +platform requirements. Update the owning repository's handoff or this coverage
[codex] +report when the new surface introduces an authenticated lookup, scanner target,
[codex] +or known standard-tool gap. Do not add a custom crawler or seed a historical
[codex] +target version merely to make discovery appear complete.
[codex] +
